cases.objective: Add group-based delegated administration: an administrator can delegate a permission to a group; members of the group, including members of nested subgroups, receive that permission; a delegation can be revoked and must take effect immediately.
cases.intended_behavior: grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) grants perms to the group and its transitive members; revoke_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) withdraws them transitively; effective_permissions(subject_id) reflects both at authorization time.
constraints: revocation must be immediate, never stale
cache use is allowed but must not serve stale data
a delegator may only delegate permissions the delegator currently holds
no new schema in scope
cases.proposed_contract: grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms); revoke_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms); effective_permissions(subject_id) -> set[perm]
open_questions: Is a 5-minute cache refresh acceptable for group membership?
Should delegation power be checked at grant time or at authorization time?

cases.objective: Add a nullable retention_hours column to the jobs table and backfill existing rows online without blocking writers.
cases.intended_behavior: Migration 0017 adds the nullable column; a backfill assigns retention_hours where it is still NULL in bounded batches; writers are never blocked; the migration is rollback-safe for existing data.
constraints: migration and backfill must be idempotent
no destructive step; rollback must not lose data for existing columns
backfill must run in bounded batches without blocking writers
cases.proposed_contract: ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN retention_hours INTEGER NULL; UPDATE jobs SET retention_hours = ? WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM jobs ORDER BY id LIMIT 1000)
open_questions: Should backfill process one batch per transaction or one transaction per row?
Is a maintenance-window backfill acceptable, or must it be online-safe?

cases.objective: Extend the public client configuration API with a timeout option while preserving behavior for existing callers.
cases.intended_behavior: connect() gains an optional timeout parameter; callers that do not pass it keep the previous effective timeout; the deprecated timeout_seconds alias remains functional during a deprecation window.
constraints: existing callers observe no silent change in effective behavior
no public symbol is removed without a deprecation window
new parameter is additive and optional
cases.proposed_contract: connect(host, port, timeout=30) -> Connection; connect(timeout_seconds=... ) remains accepted and logs a deprecation warning
open_questions: Should the deprecation warning be emitted once per process or per call?
